text:
Michael Misa scored 62 goals in his last OHL season, went second overall in 2025 right behind Matthew Schaefer, and is now the subject of trade-rumor headlines (a reported Misa-for-Simon Edvinsson talk that Detroit supposedly wants more for). At 19. That's a lot of noise around a player who is just finding his footing.

On the ice, the opportunity is growing. With Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov out, Misa has moved onto Macklin Celebrini's wing and up to about 16:40 a night, and he took Ivar Stenberg's spot on the first power-play unit. He has 10 points in 19 games, seven in his last ten.

The caution is the same as for every young Shark: San Jose has taken only 37% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and his 18.2% shooting won't last. Our range has him at 35 to 57 points over a full season, and the top-four picks he's compared with averaged 0.56 points a game in their first full year. He's at 0.53. Whatever happens with the rumors, this is the first real look at what he is next to an elite center.
headline: Misa gets his look beside Celebrini
